growth_towns.name: Hoskote
growth_towns.risks: Tamil Nadu section of the Chennai expressway faces indefinite delay.
growth_towns.why: The 80 km Dobaspet–Hoskote STRR stretch is operational and Karnataka's 71-km expressway section was reported opened; the remaining 21 km of STRR is targeted for November 2026.

growth_towns.name: Devanahalli
growth_towns.risks: Suburban rail now committed for December 2028; Blue Line opening moved to March 2028.
growth_towns.why: Airport-adjacent market where suburban rail Corridor 1 alignment has been approved by Indian Railways, with joint land measurement under way.

growth_towns.name: Doddaballapur
growth_towns.risks: Investment is at MoU stage; job and land allotment targets are plans.
growth_towns.why: KWIN City is a 5,800-acre project, and Toyota Kirloskar plans a Rs 1,200 crore BizIntel Hub there; a plotted project sold 233 plots.

growth_towns.name: Nelamangala
growth_towns.risks: Kunigal–Nelamangala is one second-airport option; no final site chosen.
growth_towns.why: Warehouse leasing led by Nelamangala and Dabaspete, with the western corridor taking 52% of leasing in H1 2026.

growth_towns.name: Bidadi
growth_towns.risks: Farmer protests, possible court action and a government review committee add uncertainty.
growth_towns.why: A GBDA-led township with 5,462 acres notified across seven villages; total footprint of 7,481 acres across nine villages is expected.

growth_towns.name: Harohalli
growth_towns.risks: Site subject to feasibility assessment; three locations still being examined.
growth_towns.why: About 40 km from the city centre, it is under consideration for a second airport on about 9,000 acres, with completion expected 2032-33.

growth_towns.name: Attibele
growth_towns.risks: Metro extension remains at feasibility report stage only.
growth_towns.why: BMRCL feasibility work covers an 11-km Yellow Line extension from Bommasandra to Attibele.

growth_towns.name: Hosur
growth_towns.risks: BMRCL says direct connection is not technically feasible; metro and airport are proposals.
growth_towns.why: Tamil Nadu is pursuing a 23-km Hosur–Bommasandra metro and plans to acquire nearly 3,000 acres for an airport.

cover_lines: Q3 sales climb as unsold stock builds
Blue Line, Pink Line and suburban rail
cover.headline: Bengaluru Builds Out: Rail, Roads and Townships
cover.subhead: Sales are recovering, launches are heavy and infrastructure timelines keep shifting. What it means for buyers across the city and its fast-growing edges.

editor_note.text: The latest quarter brought a firmer market. According to ANAROCK, Bengaluru housing sales rose 12% YoY to 16,670 units in Q3 2026. The agency also says MMR and Bengaluru together accounted for 48% of total sales across the seven cities it tracks, a reminder of how much national demand now rests on these two markets.

Jobs continue to underpin that demand. Colliers says Bengaluru led Jan-Sep 2026 office leasing at 15.7 million sq ft, driven partly by GCCs and flex operators. ANAROCK adds that GCCs made up 70% of the roughly 10.8 million sq ft of office absorption in H1 2026. Where offices cluster, housing follows.

Infrastructure is the other half of the story, and timelines deserve a careful read. BMRCL's Blue Line has reached 72% overall construction progress, per Business Today, yet Construction World reports the full opening has slipped to March 2028. K-RIDE says it is committed to starting suburban rail operations by December 2028. Buy for today's connectivity, not tomorrow's.
